title: Signal Sifter (hg38)
bodyHtml:
The Signal Sifter allows you to view significantly associated variants in a genomic region of interest, from GWAS for primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG; Gharahkhani et al., 2021) or intraocular pressure (IOP; Khawaja et al., 2018) integrated with eQTL results from Hamel et al., 2024, in the context of thousands of tissue-specific genomic annotations. 

  • Start by selecting a phenotype and ancestry. Cross-ancestry and European ancestry associations are available for POAG; only European ancestry results are available for IOP. Next, enter a gene name or genomic coordinates in the GRCh38 build (in the format "chr:start-end", e.g. "6:25413381-34403276") in the Set region box and click Search.
  • Click on a column header in the tables below to sort the table by that column.
  • Click on the "camera" icon at the upper right of each section to prepare the data in that section for downloading. Then click on the "Data files" icon at the upper right of this page to see the list of the data files you requested and download them in .csv and/or JSON format.
  • To generate a summary of the results you have viewed, click Open Summary Section at the lower right of the page and select the data types you would like to include in a summary table.

The Associated variants in region tab displays LD-clumped genetic associations for the phenotype, ancestry, and region you have selected. Filter both the plot and table using the filters below.

 

The eQTLs: by Region tab displays the locations of eQTLs (from Hamel et al., 2024) in the region you are viewing. On the Grouped by tissues tab, hover over the eGenes shown above the tracks to highlight eQTLs for those genes. On the Grouped by linked genes tab, hover over the tissue names above the tracks to highlight eQTLs for that tissue. Hover over a tissue name in the table and click Set region to open a plot below that displays links between genes and genomic regions in specific biosamples, determined by chromatin interaction experiments.

 

The plots and table on the Globally Enriched Tissues/Annotations tab display global enrichment of SLE genetic associations within regions annotated in specific tissues as accessible chromatin, binding sites, enhancers, or promoters, as determined by stratified LD score regression. Mouse over the plots to see tissue specificity.

 

The Tissue-level annotations tab displays tissue-specific epigenomic annotations in this region, drawn from the Common Metabolic Diseases Genome Atlas (CMDGA). To see annotations in specific biosamples within a tissue, mouse over a tissue name in the table, click on Set tissue, and then view the Biosample-level annotations tab.

 

The Biosample-level annotations tab displays cell type (biosample)-specific epigenomic annotations in this region for the tissue(s) you have set.

 

The Target gene links tab displays annotations from the Common Metabolic Diseases Genome Atlas (CMDGA) that are based on chromatin interactions, discovered by techniques such as ChIP-seq or Hi-C. These annotations describe genomic regions that interact (in 3-dimensional space) with specific genes in specific tissues.

 

The SNP to Gene Links tab displays genomic regions that are linked to specific genes by the Combined SNP-to-Gene strategy (Gazal et al., 2022). These links are not tissue-specific.
